exposure: Gestational age at delivery (early term, full term, late term)
cohort: Low-risk pregnancies from two northeastern US states between 1992 and 2014
finding: Continuous electronic fetal monitoring (CEFM) was independently associated with an increased risk for primary cesarean delivery and assisted vaginal births, but was not associated with a reduced risk for infant mortality in term births.
mod_finding: Use of continuous electronic fetal monitoring was independently associated with an increased risk for cesarean delivery and assisted vaginal births.
